name: Sequence: Alphanumeric Shift

hints.text: The letter skips one alphabet forward. The number skips one odd number forward.

name: Spatial: Geometric Lock

name: Cryptography: Alternating Channels
problem_statement: Directive: The string was transmitted across two alternating frequency channels. Reconstruct the message.

hints.text: This is a Rail Fence cipher. Write the letters zig-zagging up and down across two lines, then read straight across.

name: Cryptography: The Keyword Shift
problem_statement: Directive: A standard Caesar shift won't work. The encryption shifts letters based on the keyword 'KEY'. Decrypt the payload.

hints.text: In a standard 2D cube net, faces separated by exactly one square are always opposite each other.

hints.text: The shift value follows the sequence of prime numbers. Shift them backwards.

hints.text: Every bold letter is a 1. Every normal letter is a 0. Convert the 5 digits to base-10.

name: Spatial: Hexagonal Topology

hints.text: Each letter points to the next adjacent letter in the chain.

name: Spatial: Fragmented Key Overlay
problem_statement: Directive: We intercepted two images of visual static. The key is fragmented across both images. Recombine them to reveal the data.

hints.text: Use your browser inspector (F12) to move one image over the other. Set its CSS to `mix-blend-mode: multiply`.

name: Cryptography: The Triple Layer
problem_statement: Directive: The payload was encrypted in three layers: First reversed, then shifted backwards by 3 (Caesar), then converted to Base64. Unpack it.

hints.text: Work strictly backwards. 1) Decode Base64. 2) Shift letters forward by 3. 3) Reverse the string.

name: Hardware: Logic Gate Circuit
problem_statement: Directive: Validate the hardware circuit. Input Alpha is 1. Input Beta is 0. Trace the current through the AND, OR, and XOR gates. What is the final output (1 or 0)?

hints.text: AND requires both to be 1. OR requires either to be 1. XOR requires them to be strictly different.

name: Sequence: Polymorphic Derivation
problem_statement: Directive: The sequence generation is polymorphic. Predict the next node.

hints.text: Find the difference between the numbers. Then find the difference between *those* differences. Stop when the difference is constant.

name: Cryptography: Digraph Substitution
problem_statement: Directive: The cipher blocks letters into pairs using a 5x5 grid based on the keyword 'HACK'. Decode the pair 'XQ'.

hints.text: This is a Playfair Cipher. Draw a 5x5 grid, fill in H-A-C-K, then the rest of the alphabet. Form a rectangle with X and Q and pick opposite corners.

name: Cryptography: The Atbash Inversion
problem_statement: Directive: Intercepted an inverted transmission. The sender mirrored the Latin alphabet across the A-Z spectrum (A becomes Z, B becomes Y), leaving numerals and symbols intact. Decrypt the secret token.

hints.text: This is an Atbash cipher. Reflect each letter across the alphabet (C becomes X, R becomes I, etc.). Symbols and digits remain in place.

name: Cryptography: Caesar Five
problem_statement: Directive: We captured a beacon transmission rotated forward by 5 positions in the alphabet. Reverse the Caesar rotation to extract the operational flag.

hints.text: Shift each letter backwards by 5 steps (or forward by 21). H shifts back to C, W shifts back to R.

name: Cryptography: Half Rotation
problem_statement: Directive: The communication channel applies an exact 13-step symmetric rotational permutation. Recover the access code.

hints.text: ROT13 rotates characters by 13 positions (half of the 26-letter alphabet). Applying ROT13 a second time restores the plaintext.

name: Protocol: Hex Stream Extraction
problem_statement: Directive: A telemetry module performed a raw hex dump of the registration token. Convert the space-delimited hexadecimal byte stream to ASCII.

hints.text: Convert each two-digit hex value into its ASCII character equivalent (0x43 is C, 0x52 is R, 0x5F is _).

name: Protocol: Continuous Wave Telegraphy
problem_statement: Directive: Intercepted an emergency CW radio pulse. Morse characters are separated by spaces and words by slashes. Decode the audio telegraphy.

hints.text: Use the international Morse code lookup table: -.-. is C, .-. is R, ..--.- is _, ...-- is 3, ..... is 5.

name: Protocol: Base64 Authorization Blob
problem_statement: Directive: An intercepted HTTP authorization header contained an encoded credential blob. Decode the Base64 stream to reveal the agent identity.

hints.text: The trailing double-equals == indicates standard Base64 padding. Decode the ASCII string directly.

name: Hardware: Logic Analyzer Octets
problem_statement: Directive: A hardware logic analyzer tapped an 8-bit parallel bus during initialization. Convert the 8-bit binary octets to ASCII text.

hints.text: Each 8-bit block represents a character in standard ASCII. 01000011 in decimal is 67, which corresponds to capital C.

name: Sequence: Alphanumeric Indices
problem_statement: Directive: Intercepted a transmission encoded with ordinal alphanumeric indices where A=1 through Z=26. Underscores and numbers delineate segments. Decode the token.

hints.text: Map each number back to its alphabet position: 3 is C, 18 is R, 25 is Y, 16 is P, 20 is T, 15 is O.

name: Spatial: Mason Cipher Grid
problem_statement: Directive: An operative marked a secret geometric grid cipher using Pigpen enclosure notations. Enclosures represent grid cell shapes and dots. Translate the symbols.

hints.text: Standard Pigpen cipher: Grid 1 (A-I), Grid 2 with dots (J-R), X-grid (S-V), X-grid with dots (W-Z). Cross-reference each geometric enclosure.

name: Protocol: Layered Hex Base64
problem_statement: Directive: The intercepted data block was serialized in two layers: first Base64 encoded, then dumped as raw hex ASCII. Unwrap both layers to extract the flag.

hints.text: Work strictly in reverse: first decode hexadecimal to ASCII bytes, then decode the resulting Base64 string.

name: Cryptography: Vigenere Polyalphabetic
problem_statement: Directive: A periodic polyalphabetic cipher was applied to encrypt this mission directive using the keyword CIPHER. Decrypt the ciphertext.

hints.text: Subtract the shift value of each keyword letter from the ciphertext letter modulo 26. C shifts by 2, I shifts by 8, P shifts by 15.

name: Cryptography: Playfair Digraph Grid
problem_statement: Directive: We intercepted digraph pairs encoded using a 5x5 Playfair matrix generated from the keyword MATRIX. Decode the pair stream.

hints.text: Use the 5x5 Playfair square with keyword MATRIX (I and J combined). For rectangle pairs, select opposite corners in the same row. For same row or column, apply circular shifts.

evidence_board.content: Key: MATRIX | Digraphs: DT WQ AP SH RV GM MI _ 42

name: Cryptography: Rail Fence Three Depth
problem_statement: Directive: The signal was transposed across three alternate tracks in a zig-zag rail fence pattern. Rebuild the original sequence.

hints.text: Reconstruct the 3-rail fence lattice. Trace top rail, middle rail, and bottom rail in a zig-zag wave across 19 characters.

name: Cryptography: Columnar Transposition
problem_statement: Directive: The message was written into a rectangular grid and read out column by column according to the alphabetical order of key CIPHER. Recover the text.

hints.text: Key CIPHER has 6 columns with alphabetical order: C(1), E(2), H(3), I(4), P(5), R(6). Write columns into a 3x6 grid and read row by row.

name: Cryptography: Affine Modular Mapping
problem_statement: Directive: The alphabet underwent modular affine transformation E(x) = (7*x + 11) mod 26. Invert the affine transformation to recover the plaintext.

hints.text: The modular multiplicative inverse of 7 mod 26 is 15 (since 7*15 = 105 = 4*26 + 1). Compute D(y) = 15*(y - 11) mod 26.

name: Cryptography: Autokey Keystream
problem_statement: Directive: An autokey cipher was used where the keystream begins with primer KEY and continues with the plaintext characters themselves. Decrypt the message.

hints.text: First decrypt with K, E, Y. The recovered letters immediately become the next key letters to decrypt subsequent characters.

name: Cryptography: Beaufort Symmetrical Cipher
problem_statement: Directive: An Italian reciprocal Beaufort cipher scrambled the transmission using key SHIELD via formula C = (K - P) mod 26. Reverse the cipher.

hints.text: Beaufort is reciprocal: P = (K - C) mod 26. Subtract the ciphertext letter from the repeated keyword letter modulo 26.

name: Cryptography: Frequency Clue Substitution
problem_statement: Directive: Intercepted a monoalphabetic substitution payload. A cryptanalyst recovered part of the alphabet mapping: B=C, O=R, W=Y, L=P, U=T, K=O. Complete the decryption.

hints.text: Substitute the crib mapping back into the ciphertext. Use English letter frequency patterns (the high-frequency digraph QU and common suffix CY) to deduce the remaining letters.

name: Spatial: Snake Route Transposition
problem_statement: Directive: The 20-character payload was written into a 4x5 matrix in boustrophedon (snake alternating) order, then read vertically by columns. Unwind the path.

hints.text: Write the 5 column groups into a 4x5 matrix. Row 0 reads L->R, Row 1 reads R<-L, Row 2 reads L->R, Row 3 reads R<-L.

name: Spatial: Polybius Coordinate Decryption
problem_statement: Directive: Intercepted numeric coordinate pairs corresponding to a 5x5 Polybius grid (where 11=A through 55=Z, I and J share 24). Extract the letters.

hints.text: The first digit is row (1-5), the second digit is column (1-5). 13 is C, 42 is R, 54 is Y, 35 is P, 44 is T, 34 is O.

name: Cryptography: RSA Small Exponent Cube
problem_statement: Directive: A faulty RSA implementation used public exponent e=3 without message padding. The ciphertext is smaller than the modulus n. Extract the plaintext message.

hints.text: Because m^3 < n, no modular wrap-around occurred. Compute the exact integer cube root of c, then convert the integer bytes to ASCII.

name: Cryptography: RSA Fermat Factorization
problem_statement: Directive: The target RSA public key modulus n was generated using two prime factors p and q that lie unusually close to each other. Factor n and decrypt ciphertext c.

hints.text: Use Fermats factorization method: let a = ceil(sqrt(n)). Check if a^2 - n is a perfect square b^2. Then p = a - b and q = a + b, compute private exponent d, and decrypt c.

name: Cryptography: Keystream Reuse Many-Time Pad
problem_statement: Directive: Two distinct messages were encrypted using the exact same one-time pad keystream. Message 1 plaintext is known to be ATTACK_AT_DAWN_53!. Recover Message 2.

hints.text: C1 XOR M1 yields the secret keystream K. Then C2 XOR K yields plaintext Message 2.

name: Protocol: Diffie-Hellman Discrete Log
problem_statement: Directive: Intercepted a Diffie-Hellman key exchange over prime p=65537 with generator g=3. Alice public key is A=28514 and Bob is B=33041. Recover the shared secret and decrypt the payload.

hints.text: Solve the discrete logarithm g^a = A mod p using trial powers or baby-step giant-step. Compute shared secret S = B^a mod p and XOR decrypt the hex payload with str(S).

name: Cryptography: Feistel Round Inversion
problem_statement: Directive: A 2-round Feistel network with round function F(R, K) = SHA256(R + K)[:len(L)] produced ciphertext blocks (L2, R2). Invert the rounds to reconstruct L0 + R0.

hints.text: In a Feistel cipher, round 2 inversion gives: R1 = L2 and L1 = R2 XOR F(R1, K2). Then round 1 gives: R0 = L1 and L0 = R1 XOR F(R0, K1).

name: Cryptography: AES-ECB Block Oracle

The oracle maps unknown block 061994A578DAF8DF405357FE875E5DFF to a 16-byte prefix, and AA15566D980F664EFC4AF929D65B85C8 to the suffix block. Reconstruct the plaintext by probing the oracle.

hints.text: In ECB mode, identical 16-byte plaintext blocks produce identical ciphertext blocks. Match intercepted blocks against the oracle dictionary.

evidence_board.content: Query prefix block yields 061994A578DAF8DF405357FE875E5DFF. Target ciphertext: 061994A578DAF8DF405357FE875E5DFF AA15566D980F664EFC4AF929D65B85C8

name: Hardware: LFSR Keystream Synchronization
problem_statement: Directive: A 5-bit LFSR with feedback polynomial x^5 + x^3 + 1 generated a pseudo-random keystream initialized with seed state [1, 0, 1, 1, 0]. Synchronize the stream and decrypt the 19-byte payload.

hints.text: Compute keystream bit feedback = s[4] XOR s[2] at each shift step starting from [1, 0, 1, 1, 0]. XOR the bitstream with the hex ciphertext bytes.

name: Protocol: Merkle-Damgard Hash Extension
problem_statement: Directive: A server signs requests as MD5(secret || message) with a 16-byte secret. Original message action=read has MD5 hash e38eb7dc7dd0602f068f80695026c2cf. An extension appends &action=admin. Compute the extended MD5 digest and XOR decrypt the payload.

hints.text: Total initial length is 16 + 11 = 27 bytes. Format the 64-byte Merkle-Damgard padding block and resume MD5 internal state from the original digest to compute the extended hash, then XOR decrypt the payload.

evidence_board.content: SecretLen: 16 | OrigMsg: action=read | OrigMD5: e38eb7dc7dd0602f068f80695026c2cf | Append: &action=admin | Payload: 4B0731A667C9A21999D5BD29DA9DF9B030

name: Cryptography: Merkle-Hellman Knapsack
problem_statement: Directive: Decrypt the Merkle-Hellman knapsack ciphertext vector. Private superincreasing sequence is w=(2, 5, 11, 25, 53, 110, 225, 455), modulus q=887, multiplier r=135 (r^-1 mod q = 381).

hints.text: Multiply each ciphertext value by r^-1 mod q (381 mod 887). Then use the greedy knapsack approach with w from 455 down to 2 to extract the 8 bits of each ASCII character.

name: Cryptography: ECC Point Multiplication
problem_statement: Directive: On elliptic curve y^2 = x^3 + 3x + 7 (mod 991), generator point G = (2, 608). Alice computes shared point P = 5*G. Coordinate key is x*1000 + y. Decrypt the ciphertext.

hints.text: Use elliptic curve group addition and doubling over F_991 to compute 5*G. Key is x*1000 + y. XOR decrypt each character with repeating digits of the key.
